Dispatching to an `os-dev` on triage's charter of 2026-08-25 19:54Z, unchanged. Recording three things the dev needs that are newer than the card:

1. **The card's ref is stale.** The probe was written and run against `origin/main` @ `591bf2791`; `main` is at `9d86e1d7` today. Re-locate every line and re-run the four cases on your own ref before writing anything — a case that fails today is a regression report back to this seat, per the charter, not a silent fix.
2. **File face is test-only, and that is a fence, not an observation.** Two other devs hold `packages/app-shell` right now — one on the package barrel and `AppContent`, one on `src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx`. Adding no export and touching no production file is what keeps this card off both of them. If you find you cannot pin a behaviour without a production edit, stop and report rather than widening.
3. **Item 4 is already pinned** at `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/DeclaredActionsBar.test.tsx` — reference it, do not restate it.

The fixture is the load-bearing part: two approver ids sharing one display name across two 会签 groups (`u_fin` Finance / `u_leg` Legal), a `flow:` submitter id, a payload carrying both `owner_id` and `amount`. A single-approver or single-group fixture passes against the pre-fix code and therefore proves nothing — each case must be shown to fail against the behaviour it pins being absent, not merely to pass today.

Charter held exactly: three behaviours pinned, **item 4 referenced and not duplicated** (`DeclaredActionsBar.test.tsx` confirmed present and correctly named), no production code touched, and `packages/app-shell` left alone per the fence — which is what kept this card off the two devs holding that package this batch.

## ⭐ The ablation is why this is a characterization suite and not three tests that happen to pass

The whole risk with a card like this is writing assertions that pass today and would keep passing through the regression they exist to catch. Four legs, each **predicted before running**, each observed to match exactly, each failing **only** the case naming that behaviour while the other two stayed green:

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `approverChips()` key dropped to label-only | the two same-name chips collapse to one | `expected … to have a length of 2 but got 1` |
| 2 | `isSystemSubmitter()` forced false | Flow-initiated disappears | `Unable to find an element with the text: Flow-initiated` |
| 3a | `prettifyKey()`'s id-token-drop line removed | label reads `Owner Id`, not `Owner` | `Unable to find an element with the text: Owner`, the failure's own DOM dump showing literal `Owner Id` |
| 3b | `payloadSummary()` no longer passed `drawerAmount?.key` as `excludeKey` | amount renders twice | `expected … to have a length of 1 but got 2` |

⭐ That per-leg isolation is the part that matters. A suite where every leg reds everything discriminates nothing; here each mutation reds exactly its own case.

And the **fixture** is the one the class needs — two approver ids (`u_fin`, `u_leg`) sharing the display name `Dev Admin` across Finance and Legal, a `flow:`-prefixed submitter with no `submitter_name`, a payload carrying both `owner_id` and `amount`. A single-approver or single-group fixture passes against the pre-fix code and proves nothing; this one cannot.

## ⭐⭐ It hit the shared-refs hazard mid-task and handled it correctly

`origin/main` advanced from `9d86e1d79` to `fff964510` **under the worktree** while the dev was working — the shared `refs/remotes/*` hazard AGENTS.md §9 names, and the exact "moving anchor" failure this lane has been bitten by before. The dev **merged** (not rebased) and re-verified everything on the merged ref before pushing. That is the right call in both halves: merge keeps a pushed branch's checkout valid, and re-verifying is what makes the green mean something about what will actually land.

## One judgement call, correct

`check-changeset-presence` demanded a declaration, so the dev wrote a **no-release (empty-frontmatter) changeset** rather than reaching for `skip-changeset`. Right on both counts — the gate's own verdict is the declaration form here, and `skip-changeset` is inert in this repo, so applying it would only have minted a false status.

⛔ Nothing was widened, nothing was fixed silently. The charter's stop condition — *a case that fails on today's `main` is a regression report, not something to fix here* — was not hit: all three pass on the merged ref, which is what makes this a characterization suite rather than a bug fix.
